Data: [TidyTuesday 2026-07-14](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2026/2026-07-14).

Beak length against beak depth is the scatter plot the palmerpenguins dataset is known for, and this week's data lets it be drawn for all 18 species instead of the usual three.
Set against the whole family, the famous trio turns out to sit in one corner of it: their beaks span 53.4 to 69.1 mm in length and 15.3 to 21.8 mm in depth, about a quarter of the family's range in one direction and a third of it in the other, so roughly 8% of the area the other fifteen species fill.
What sits outside that box is most of what a penguin beak can be, from the 43.5 mm bill of the little penguin to the 110 mm of the king penguin, and the 31 mm depth of the royal penguin.
